title: Lifecycle Email Nurture Sequence Copy — Latency/$ Benchmark Report (v1.3)
content:
Doc purpose
- Draft copy for a 4–5 touch lifecycle sequence supporting the public-facing “Latency per Dollar” benchmark report launch.
- Primary KPI: report downloads + qualified “talk to us” conversions (Hosted API → Dedicated/Private).
- Secondary KPI: reply rate from high-intent leads with region + workload details.

Owner / approvals
- Owner: Ben Carter
- Messaging review: Soojin Lee
- Technical review (methodology wording, disclaimers): Markus Klein + Ethan Wallace
- Ops/UTM + send rules: Tyler Benson
- EMEA residency language check: Lukas Meyer
- CS alignment (inbound routing expectations): Jasmine Liu

Audience + segmentation (ops notes)
1) Segment A — Self-serve / PLG
- Who: trial + free credit signups, API key created, < 30 days, low-to-medium usage
- Goal: drive report download + quickstart to run the same workload on Redwood
- Tone: technical, fast, “here’s how to think about latency/$”

2) Segment B — Sales-assisted / enterprise
- Who: demo requests, Dedicated/Private interest, high volume usage, security questionnaire started
- Goal: get a meeting scheduled, arm champions with methodology credibility
- Tone: slightly more structured, procurement-friendly, mention regions/data residency carefully

3) Segment C — Existing customers
- Who: active customers
- Goal: keep informed + prompt expansion conversations; avoid “sell-y” emails
- Tone: “FYI + what’s new + how to interpret; office hours”
- NOTE: For Segment C, replace “Book a consult” with “Office hours / review your workload” and route to CSM.

From name / reply-to (suggested)
- From: “Redwood Inference” (or “Ethan at Redwood” for Email #2 if we want a more technical voice)
- Reply-to: monitored alias (marketing-ops will set) + auto-route high-intent replies to SDR/AE owner.

Link + UTM conventions (Tyler)
- Base campaign: utm_campaign=benchmark_report_2025q1
- Medium: utm_medium=email
- Source: utm_source=customerio (or hubspot, depending on tool)
- Content: utm_content=email1_announcement / email2_methodology / email3_spotlight / email4_consult / email5_officehours
- Term: optional for segment (utm_term=plg / enterprise / customer)

Compliance / claims guardrails (copy reminders)
- Avoid “fastest” / “best” blanket claims.
- Use “measured under the methodology described” + “results vary by workload, region, and configuration.”
- Emphasize reproducibility + constraints.
- Don’t imply we used customer data. (We didn’t; keep language explicit.)

Personalization tokens (implement as available)
- {{first_name}}
- {{company}}
- {{primary_region}} (if known)
- {{use_case}} (if known)
- {{owner_name}} (AE/CSM)

========================================
EMAIL #1 — Launch announcement (Day 0)
========================================

Send timing
- Day 0 after report goes live (same day as blog + landing page)
- Segment A/B: yes
- Segment C: optional, but keep it short and informational

Subject line (A/B)
A) New benchmark: Latency per dollar across models + regions
B) We measured “latency/$” for popular open models (report)
C) Benchmark report: production economics for LLM inference

Preview text
- A region-by-region look at throughput, p95 latency, and cost — plus methodology + reproducibility notes.

Body (default)
Hi {{first_name}},

We just published a new benchmark report focused on production economics for LLM inference: **latency per dollar**.

What’s inside:
- Results broken down **by model family and cloud region** (NA/EU + APAC)
- Supporting metrics (throughput + latency distribution) so you can reason about real-world behavior
- A clear methodology section (workloads, concurrency, warmup/caching policy) to make the numbers interpretable

If you’re building an LLM feature in production, latency/$ is a useful way to compare options because it ties performance directly to spend — not just raw speed or cost in isolation.

**Download the report:** {{report_download_link}}?utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=benchmark_report_2025q1&utm_content=email1_announcement&utm_term={{segment}}

If you reply with your region + rough traffic shape (concurrency + typical input/output length), we can point you to the most relevant tables.

— Redwood Inference

Footer note (small)
Results reflect the methodology described in the report and are intended to be directional. Performance can vary based on workload, configuration, and regional capacity.

CTA buttons (if using buttons)
- Primary: Download the report
- Secondary: View methodology

Variant for Segment B (enterprise add-on paragraph)
If you’re evaluating Dedicated or Private deployment options, we can also share how to map these results to your requirements (SLOs, data residency, isolation, and predictable throughput).

========================================
EMAIL #2 — Methodology deep dive (Day 3)
========================================

Goal
- Build credibility and reduce “benchmarketing” skepticism.
- Drive engagement with methodology appendix + reproducibility example.

Subject line (A/B)
A) How we measured latency/$ (and how to reproduce it)
B) Benchmark methodology: what we controlled (and what we didn’t)
C) What “latency per dollar” means in practice

Preview text
- Workloads, distributions, reruns/variance checks, and interpretation notes.

Body
Hi {{first_name}},

Following up on the latency/$ report — a few notes on **how** we ran it, since methodology is the difference between a useful benchmark and a misleading one.

Key choices (high level):
1) **Workloads:** chat + embeddings baselines (representative prompt sets and output targets)
2) **Concurrency + distribution:** measured under defined load profiles (not a single “hero run”)
3) **Warmup + caching policy:** explicitly stated so the results aren’t accidentally “best case only”
4) **Variance + reruns:** repeat runs with thresholds and rerun rules to catch infra noise
5) **Reporting:** we include latency distributions and throughput context — not just one number

We’ve also documented limitations and how to interpret differences across regions.

**Read the methodology appendix:** {{methodology_link}}?utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=benchmark_report_2025q1&utm_content=email2_methodology&utm_term={{segment}}

If you want to sanity-check the benchmark against your own workload, here’s a smaller reproduction guide:
**Reproduce a subset of the benchmark:** {{reproduce_link}}?utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=benchmark_report_2025q1&utm_content=email2_methodology_reproduce&utm_term={{segment}}

If you tell us:
- target region(s)
- typical input tokens / output tokens
- target p95 latency
…we can recommend the most relevant comparison points.

— Ethan Wallace (Redwood Inference)

Footer note (small)
Benchmarks are directional and constrained by the workloads and configurations described. We avoid publishing any customer-identifying telemetry.

========================================
EMAIL #3 — Region/model spotlight (Day 7)
========================================

Goal
- Make the report feel actionable (not just “interesting”).
- Nudge readers to the right region table and remind them regional deltas are real.

Subject line (A/B)
A) Region spotlight: what changes across NA/EU/APAC
B) Picking a region + model: a quick way to use the tables
C) Benchmark tables: find your region + model in 2 minutes

Preview text
- A simple way to compare options without overfitting to one chart.

Body (default)
Hi {{first_name}},

A common question we’ve gotten since publishing the latency/$ report is: “How much does region actually matter?”

The short version: **it can matter a lot**, and not always in the way you expect — especially once you factor in routing policy, capacity, and your latency SLO.

Here’s a simple workflow to use the report:
1) Start with your **primary user region** (or your data residency requirement)
2) In that region table, narrow to a **model family** that fits your quality needs
3) Compare options using **latency/$ + p95 latency + throughput context** (don’t optimize on a single metric)

Quick links to tables (edit links to the final anchors):
- North America tables: {{na_tables_link}}?utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=benchmark_report_2025q1&utm_content=email3_spotlight_na&utm_term={{segment}}
- Europe tables: {{eu_tables_link}}?utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=benchmark_report_2025q1&utm_content=email3_spotlight_eu&utm_term={{segment}}
- APAC tables: {{apac_tables_link}}?utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=benchmark_report_2025q1&utm_content=email3_spotlight_apac&utm_term={{segment}}

If you reply with:
- “chat” or “embeddings”
- target region(s)
- concurrency range
…we’ll point you to the 2–3 rows in the table that most closely match what you’re doing.

— Redwood Inference

EMEA-friendly language addendum (Segment B or EMEA)
If you have EU data residency requirements, we recommend starting with the EU table and validating with a small reproduction run using your own prompt distribution.

========================================
EMAIL #4 — Book a consult / map to your workload (Day 12)
========================================

Goal
- Convert engaged readers to a meeting.
- Frame consult as “mapping report → your SLO + cost target,” not a generic sales call.

Subject line (A/B)
A) Want help mapping latency/$ to your workload?
B) Benchmark results are directional — let’s size this for your SLO
C) Dedicated vs Hosted: how to use the report to choose

Preview text
- Share your region + throughput targets and we’ll recommend a configuration (Hosted, Dedicated, or Private).

Body
Hi {{first_name}},

If you’re trying to turn benchmark numbers into a real deployment decision, the missing step is usually connecting:
- your region + routing constraints
- your workload shape (concurrency + token distribution)
- your SLO (especially p95) and reliability requirements
- your unit-cost target

If you want, we can do a **20-minute consult** and walk through:
- which models/regions from the report best match your constraints
- how to reproduce a subset with your prompts
- when Hosted API is enough vs when Dedicated/Private makes sense

**Book a time:** {{book_consult_link}}?utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=benchmark_report_2025q1&utm_content=email4_consult&utm_term={{segment}}

Prefer async? Reply with your region(s), target p95, and rough usage (tokens/day). We’ll respond with recommended next steps.

— {{owner_name}} (Redwood Inference)

Segment C (existing customer) alternate CTA
Instead of “Book a time,” use:
**Join office hours:** {{office_hours_link}}?utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=benchmark_report_2025q1&utm_content=email4_officehours&utm_term=customer
And route to the CSM.

========================================
EMAIL #5 (OPTIONAL) — Office hours / last call (Day 20)
========================================

When to use
- If engagement is high but meeting conversion is low.
- If we want a lower-friction CTA for engineers.

Subject line options
A) Office hours: bring your region + workload, we’ll sanity-check latency/$
B) Last call: benchmark Q&A + reproduction walkthrough

Preview text
- Live Q&A with Perf/Evals + Solutions Engineering.

Body
Hi {{first_name}},

We’re hosting a short office hours session for anyone using the latency/$ report to make deployment decisions.

Agenda (30 minutes):
- How to interpret latency/$ vs throughput vs p95
- What changes across regions (and why)
- How to reproduce a subset with your own prompt distribution

**Save your seat:** {{office_hours_link}}?utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=benchmark_report_2025q1&utm_content=email5_officehours&utm_term={{segment}}

If you can’t make it, reply with your region + SLO and we’ll follow up async.

— Redwood Inference

========================================
Operational notes / TODOs
========================================
- Confirm final canonical URLs for: report download, methodology appendix, region tables, reproduction guide, booking link.
- Implement suppression rules:
  - suppress if bounced/unsubscribed
  - suppress “Book consult” for existing customers with active CSM motion (route to office hours or CSM email)
  - suppress if already scheduled meeting from Email #1
- Ensure consistent disclaimer language across all emails (avoid over-claiming).
- Localization: keep English-only for this launch; EMEA wording review is about residency language, not translation.

Open questions
1) Do we want Email #2 to come from “Ethan” for higher technical credibility, or keep consistent “Redwood Inference” brand sender?
2) Should we include one lightweight “table snippet” image in Email #3, or keep purely text to reduce rendering issues?
3) Do we want a split path based on click behavior (methodology clickers get more technical follow-up; table clickers get consult CTA sooner)?

Change log
- v1.3 (2025-02-14): Added EMEA residency addendum + clarified Segment C alternate CTA (office hours). Added UTM content naming conventions.
- v1.2 (2025-02-10): Tightened claims language; added reproducibility link in Email #2.
